decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with left arm to the horizontal mallet; rotate gradually toward a downward grasp, keeping right arm parked.
Move above the mallet handle while continuing the wrist turn to match its left-to-right axis.
Align the open left gripper over the handle near its tail, maintaining overhead clearance before final descent.
Use wrist view to center the shaft and lower cautiously to the grasp height; the handle is still right of the gripper center.
Fine-align with the shaft and close the left gripper around the handle; retention will be checked with a small lift.
Keep the handle clamped and lift vertically to verify that the mallet follows before approaching the first key.
The mallet follows the closed gripper. Carry it above the leftmost red key with clearance, keeping the left hand on the left side.
Center the mallet head over the lower-middle of the leftmost red key, then lower cautiously for the first strike.
Finish the downward tap on the leftmost red key, then lift the mallet by 4 cm before moving to the next key.
Move the raised mallet one key to the right and tap the second, orange key; keep the grip closed and the right arm clear.
Lift clear of the orange key by 4.8 cm, then position over the third, yellow key for the next downward tap.
Tap the third yellow key vertically, then lift 5.5 cm to separate the strike from the next note.
Advance the raised mallet to the fourth, green key and lower for its strike, maintaining the left elbow-up posture.
Lift the mallet 5.5 cm from the green key before shifting right to the fifth, cyan key.
Strike the fifth cyan key and lift vertically by 5.7 cm while retaining the mallet.
Move above the sixth, blue key and make the next downward strike, keeping the closed grip and left-arm workspace.
Lift 5.5 cm clear of the sixth blue key, then shift to the seventh purple key without crossing the arms.
Slightly center the tip over the seventh purple key, tap downward, then lift 5.6 cm before the final key.
Move to the rightmost eighth magenta key and strike vertically; the mallet remains held by the left hand.
Lift vertically clear of the final magenta key by 8 cm, exceeding the required post-strike separation while keeping the mallet held.
The planned eight-key pass is finished, but contact completion is not confirmed. Return above the left side with generous clearance for a deliberate verification pass.
Align over the middle of the leftmost red bar, farther from its end fastener, while retaining clearance for a fresh left-to-right pass.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments, centering and lowering the mallet toward the middle of the red bar.
Complete a centered red-key tap, lift 5.6 cm clear, and advance the raised mallet to the orange key.
The tip appears left of the orange bar after lifting. Correct its horizontal alignment from RGB, then lower cautiously onto the orange center.
Finish the orange-key contact, lift 5.2 cm, then advance over the yellow key while checking the retained mallet alignment.
Tap the centered third yellow bar, then lift 6 cm vertically so the next note is distinctly separated.
Adjust the fourth green-key target using the current tip position, then approach more shallowly to avoid excessive contact deflection.
Complete the centered green tap, lift 5.6 cm, and move above the fifth cyan key for the next strike.
Strike the fifth cyan bar with a brief contact pause, then lift 6 cm before proceeding to blue.
Advance one key right to blue, lower the tip onto its middle, and briefly pause at contact before lifting.
Lift 6 cm off blue while easing out the small contact deflection, then move the raised tip to the seventh purple key.
Tap the seventh purple bar vertically, then lift 6 cm to separate it from the final magenta note.
Advance to the rightmost magenta key and make the final centered tap with a brief contact pause.
Lift 8 cm after the final magenta strike, retaining the mallet and avoiding any further key contact.
The final tip lift is visible. Retract the held mallet above the table and away from the keys, maintaining clearance and elbow-up continuity.
Move to a clear left-side holding position with the mallet raised; avoid further contact after the left-to-right sequence.
Hold the mallet securely in the clear left-side position after the final lift; no additional key contact.
